relevant_findings.finding: Two fundamentally different substrates share the 'stucco' label. Traditional 3-coat stucco: Portland cement/sand/lime, 7/8 to 1 inch thick, ~10 lbs/SF, pH up to 13 on new installations. EIFS (Exterior Insulation and Finish System): expanded polystyrene (EPS) insulation board + polymer-modified base coat + reinforcing mesh + 100% acrylic finish coat, ~2 lbs/SF. These substrates require DIFFERENT coating systems — a coating appropriate for one may catastrophically fail on the other.

relevant_findings.topic: New stucco cure requirements and accelerated coating
relevant_findings.finding: Traditional stucco requires 28-30 day standard cure to allow cement hydration to stabilize and pH to lower through carbonation. Accelerated coating is possible as early as 7 days using alkali-resistant primer (e.g., SW Loxon-type) rated to withstand pH up to 13. The 7-day accelerated path is the primary NC scenario since construction schedules rarely allow 30-day delays. EIFS has no alkalinity cure requirement — the acrylic finish coat cures in 24-48 hours.

relevant_findings.topic: Crack assessment protocol — hard stop at 1/8 inch
relevant_findings.finding: Crack assessment is mandatory before coating stucco. Cracks less than 1/8 inch are cosmetic — patch with elastomeric caulk or bridge with elastomeric coating. Cracks greater than 1/8 inch indicate STRUCTURAL movement — this is a HARD STOP requiring structural assessment before any coating work. Do not coat over structural cracks. This applies to both traditional stucco and EIFS.

relevant_findings.topic: Elastomeric coating — traditional stucco ONLY, NEVER on EIFS
relevant_findings.finding: Elastomeric coatings (12-20 mils DFT, >300% elongation) are designed for traditional stucco to bridge hairline cracks. They are STRICTLY PROHIBITED on EIFS. Elastomeric on EIFS traps moisture behind the insulation board, leading to substrate deterioration, mold growth, and catastrophic system failure. This is the single most critical material routing rule in this spec: coating_system = elastomeric is LOCKED OUT when substrate_type = EIFS.

EIFS requires 100% acrylic coatings that are flexible and vapor-permeable. The coating must allow moisture vapor transmission to prevent entrapment behind the EPS board. Additionally, EIFS color selection is constrained by Light Reflectance Value (LRV): LRV must be >20 (preferably >50). Low LRV (dark colors) absorb excessive solar heat, causing EPS expansion/contraction that can delaminate the system. Dark colors on EIFS void most manufacturer warranties.

relevant_findings.topic: Pressure washing — dramatically different by substrate type
relevant_findings.finding: Traditional stucco: 1,500-3,000 PSI water wash for cleaning. Stucco can handle moderate pressure. EIFS: LOWEST possible pressure settings only — high pressure damages the thin acrylic finish coat and can penetrate to the EPS board, introducing moisture into the wall system. EIFS cleaning should use garden hose pressure with soft brush, or maximum 500 PSI with wide fan tip at 24+ inch distance.

Both stucco types are susceptible to mildew growth, particularly on north-facing elevations and areas with poor drainage. Mildew must be completely eradicated before coating — painting over mildew causes adhesion failure and mildew regrowth through the new film. Treatment: bleach solution (1:3 household bleach to water), dwell 15-20 minutes, scrub with stiff brush, rinse thoroughly. Allow to dry completely before coating.

Traditional stucco (cementitious) can develop efflorescence — white powdery salt deposits from moisture evaporation through the alkaline substrate. Treatment follows the same masonry protocol: water + stiff brush (light) -> TSP (moderate) -> phosphoric acid (severe). Muriatic acid as last resort with pre-dampening, neutralization, and thorough rinsing. Efflorescence indicates moisture intrusion that must be corrected before coating. EIFS does not develop efflorescence (non-cite substrate).

Spray on stucco = auto-add backroll. Stucco texture creates voids and shadowed areas that spray alone cannot fully penetrate. Back-rolling forces coating into texture recesses for continuous film and proper DFT. This is MANDATORY per Application Methods Doctrine. Spray-only on stucco is NOT acceptable. Roller nap selection driven by texture: smooth 3/4-1 inch, sand 1-1/4 inch, lace/dash 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch.

relevant_findings.topic: Texture profile drives production rate AND material consumption
relevant_findings.finding: Stucco texture profile is the dominant production and material driver. Production rates (SF/hr): smooth 125-150, sand 80-100, lace 60-80, dash/roughcast 40-60. Material coverage (SF/gal): smooth 300-350, sand 200-250, lace 150-200, dash/roughcast 75-125. Texture creates a dual multiplier effect — rougher textures BOTH slow production AND increase material consumption. This is the key estimating insight for stucco.

EIFS inspection requires 'knock test' — tapping the surface to detect hollow areas indicating delamination between the EPS board and the base coat, or between the base coat and the finish coat. Hollow areas indicate moisture intrusion or adhesive failure. Widespread delamination is a HARD STOP — substrate repair required before coating. Isolated delamination spots can be routed and patched.

Commercial General Liability (CGL) insurance policies commonly exclude EIFS-related work or EIFS-related claims. Before accepting EIFS coating work, the contractor must verify: (1) insurance coverage includes EIFS, or (2) obtain an EIFS-specific rider. Photo documentation of pre-existing conditions is MANDATORY for EIFS work. This is a business/liability flag, not an estimation factor, but must be surfaced in the project workflow.

relevant_findings.topic: ASTM D3359 adhesion test for previously coated stucco
relevant_findings.finding: For stucco that has been previously coated (repaint context), ASTM D3359 cross-hatch adhesion test is required to verify existing coating adhesion. For NC stucco, this test is not applicable since there is no existing coating. However, the adhesion test protocol should be documented in SOP for future reference if the field crew encounters unexpected existing coatings on 'new' stucco.

relevant_findings.topic: Stucco patch and repair before coating
relevant_findings.finding: New construction stucco may have minor defects from the plastering process: trowel marks, cold joints, rough patches, or minor cracks from initial shrinkage. These require patching before coating. Traditional stucco: patch with stucco patch compound matching existing texture. EIFS: patch with manufacturer-specified base coat and texture match. Patch areas must cure before priming (traditional: 7+ days, EIFS: per manufacturer).

condition_drivers.impact: The primary branching dimension. Drives coating system selection (elastomeric allowed on traditional ONLY, EIFS = acrylic ONLY), pressure wash settings (1,500-3,000 PSI traditional vs <500 PSI EIFS), primer requirements (alkali-resistant for traditional, standard acrylic for EIFS), LRV constraints (EIFS only: LRV >20), and insurance/liability requirements (EIFS only: CGL rider).
condition_drivers.notes: This is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION. The two substrate types are fundamentally different materials that happen to share a visual category. Coating system compatibility is a HARD CONSTRAINT, not a preference.

condition_drivers.impact: Drives BOTH production rate AND material consumption — dual multiplier. Smooth: 125-150 SF/hr, 300-350 SF/gal (baseline). Sand: 80-100 SF/hr, 200-250 SF/gal (1.25x labor, 1.25x material). Lace (Spanish lace): 60-80 SF/hr, 150-200 SF/gal (1.50x labor, 1.50x material). Dash/roughcast: 40-60 SF/hr, 75-125 SF/gal (2.00x labor, 2.00x material). Also drives roller nap selection.
condition_drivers.notes: This is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION. Texture multiplier is BOTH a labor rate modifier (affects production SF/hr) AND a material consumption modifier (affects coverage SF/gal). Both pathways needed per RC-006.

condition_drivers.impact: Elastomeric: 12-20 mils DFT, >300% elongation, bridges hairline cracks — traditional stucco ONLY. Coverage 100-175 SF/gal. Acrylic: 4-6 mils DFT, flexible, vapor permeable, UV resistant — required for EIFS, preferred for sound traditional stucco. Coverage 200-350 SF/gal. CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: elastomeric is PROHIBITED on EIFS (hard blocker).
condition_drivers.notes: This is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION. When substrate_type = EIFS, coating_system MUST be locked to acrylic. Elastomeric selection is only valid when substrate_type = traditional_stucco. This is enforced as a hard constraint rule, not a recommendation.

condition_drivers.impact: QT2: economy — light wash, single finish coat on primed surface, economy 100% acrylic. QT3: standard — full wash, dedicated primer, two finish coats, mid-grade acrylic or elastomeric. QT4: premium — TSP wash, premium primer, two finish coats with premium materials, raking light inspection between coats, texture-matching patch verification.
condition_drivers.notes: QT5 not applicable to stucco wall field — reserved for fine exterior millwork only. QT2 may accept single finish coat on properly primed stucco if substrate is sound.

condition_drivers.impact: Spray_backroll is the primary method for stucco field surfaces. Roll is the fallback for smaller areas or occupied-adjacent. Brush is for detail work and small patches only. IMPORTANT: spray on stucco ALWAYS requires backroll — there is no spray-only option. Spray_backroll requires 2-person crew.
condition_drivers.notes: This is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION. spray_backroll forces coating into texture recesses. Roll provides excellent mechanical bond. Brush is never the primary method for stucco wall field.

condition_drivers.impact: Height modifier on all tasks at elevation. ground=1.00, ladder=1.35, scaffold=1.60, lift=1.50. Applied per elevation based on working height. Scaffold common for multi-story stucco (long continuous runs at height).
condition_drivers.notes: Treated as a HEIGHT MODIFIER (like FAC_HEIGHT for interior), not a site condition. A project may have ground access on one elevation and scaffold on another.

quality_differences.description: Economy exterior stucco. Light water wash. Alkali-resistant primer on traditional stucco (still mandatory — pH hazard is not quality-optional). Standard acrylic primer on EIFS. Single finish coat acceptable on properly primed surface. Economy-grade 100% acrylic exterior. No edge precision required. Patch only obvious defects.
quality_differences.typical_use: Commercial/retail stucco, rental property, budget-constrained. Crack assessment still mandatory at QT2.

quality_differences.description: Standard residential stucco. Full water wash (pressure-appropriate to substrate type). Mildew eradication if present. Efflorescence treatment on traditional stucco if present. Crack assessment and patching. Dedicated primer (alkali-resistant for traditional, acrylic for EIFS). Two finish coats with mid-grade product. Clean transitions at trim/window interfaces. Caulk stucco-to-trim joints.
quality_differences.typical_use: Standard homeowner NC stucco, most residential exterior stucco painting.

quality_differences.description: Premium exterior stucco. Full TSP wash. Complete mildew eradication. Efflorescence treatment. Premium primer. Two finish coats with premium materials (SW Duration, BM Aura Exterior). Raking light inspection before second coat. Texture-matching verification on patches. Crisp trim lines. EIFS: full knock test documentation with photo evidence.
quality_differences.typical_use: High-end residential, custom homes, architectural stucco where coating quality is paramount.

failure_modes.name: Saponification on uncured traditional stucco
failure_modes.description: Traditional stucco is Portland cement-based with pH up to 13 on new installations. Standard coatings applied to uncured alkaline stucco suffer chemical binder destruction. Alkaline hydroxides attack pigments and binders, causing color loss, soft/sticky films, and total coating failure. Oil-based products suffer immediate saponification — hydrolysis of esters into soap.
failure_modes.prevention: Use alkali-resistant primer rated to pH 13 (e.g., SW Loxon Masonry Primer) on all new traditional stucco. NEVER use oil-based or alkyd products on stucco. Verify cure age (30-day standard, 7-day minimum with Loxon-type primer).
failure_modes.detection: Soft, sticky paint film. Color loss or yellowing. Film peels off in sheets. Chalky residue on oil-based products.

failure_modes.name: EIFS moisture entrapment from elastomeric coating
failure_modes.description: Elastomeric coatings applied to EIFS trap moisture behind the EPS insulation board. Unlike traditional stucco which can tolerate some moisture diffusion through its mass, EIFS relies on the coating system to manage vapor transmission. Elastomeric films (low permeability) seal the exterior face, trapping condensation and incidental water between the coating and the EPS. This leads to mold growth, EPS deterioration, adhesive failure, and catastrophic system delamination.
failure_modes.prevention: NEVER apply elastomeric coatings on EIFS. This is a HARD BLOCKER RULE. EIFS = 100% acrylic only (flexible, vapor permeable). Enforce at material selection stage — no exceptions.
failure_modes.detection: Blistering or bubbling on EIFS surface. Soft spots when pressed. Musty odor at wall penetrations. Visible mold at edges or penetrations. Delamination of finish coat from base coat.

failure_modes.name: Crack bridging failure — elastomeric over structural cracks
failure_modes.description: Elastomeric coatings can bridge hairline cracks (<1/8 inch) through elongation (>300%). However, if applied over active structural cracks (>1/8 inch), ongoing substrate movement exceeds the coating's elongation capacity. The coating tears at the crack location, exposing the substrate to accelerated moisture intrusion at the exact point of structural weakness.
failure_modes.prevention: Mandatory crack assessment before coating. Cracks >1/8 inch = HARD STOP for structural assessment. Do not rely on elastomeric coating to solve structural crack issues. Patch cosmetic cracks (<1/8 inch) with elastomeric caulk before coating.
failure_modes.detection: Visible crack re-opening through coating film. Coating tears along crack lines. Moisture staining at crack locations after rain events.

failure_modes.name: Efflorescence recurrence on traditional stucco
failure_modes.description: Salt deposits push through the coating film from behind on traditional cementitious stucco. Indicates ongoing moisture intrusion that the coating alone cannot solve. Efflorescence returns even after cleaning if the moisture source is not corrected. Coating over active efflorescence causes immediate adhesion failure.
failure_modes.prevention: Identify and correct moisture source before coating. Remove all existing efflorescence with appropriate method (water/TSP/acid progression). Do not coat over active efflorescence. Document moisture source assessment.
failure_modes.detection: White crystalline deposits on or under paint film. Paint blistering with white powder underneath. Recurring salt deposits after cleaning.

failure_modes.name: Adhesion failure from inadequate surface preparation
failure_modes.description: Stucco surfaces with mildew, efflorescence, form-release residue, or insufficient cleaning develop poor adhesion. The coating appears sound initially but delaminates in sheets within months, typically triggered by moisture cycling or thermal expansion. Particularly common when mildew is painted over — mildew organisms prevent mechanical bond and regrow through the film.
failure_modes.prevention: Full cleaning protocol appropriate to substrate type. Mildew eradication mandatory (bleach solution, dwell, scrub, rinse). Efflorescence treatment on traditional stucco. Verify surface is clean, dry, and dull before priming.
failure_modes.detection: Coating peeling in sheets (not flaking). Mildew visible through or under coating. Adhesion test failure (ASTM D3359 cross-hatch).

failure_modes.name: EIFS delamination from high-pressure washing
failure_modes.description: EIFS finish coat is a thin acrylic layer (~1/16 inch) over reinforcing mesh and base coat. High-pressure washing (>500 PSI or close-distance) can puncture or delaminate this finish layer, introducing water directly into the EPS board. Moisture-saturated EPS loses insulation value and creates conditions for mold growth and system failure.
failure_modes.prevention: EIFS cleaning: garden hose pressure with soft brush, or maximum 500 PSI with wide fan tip at 24+ inch distance. NEVER use standard pressure washer settings (1,500-3,000 PSI) on EIFS. Train crew to identify EIFS before washing.
failure_modes.detection: Visible damage to finish coat surface after washing. Soft/spongy areas. Water weeping from EIFS joints or penetrations hours after washing.

failure_modes.name: EIFS thermal distress from low LRV colors
failure_modes.description: Dark colors (LRV <20) absorb excessive solar radiation, heating the EIFS surface to 160-180 degrees F. EPS foam softens above 165 degrees F. Repeated thermal cycling causes EPS expansion/contraction beyond system tolerances, leading to base coat cracking, finish coat crazing, and eventual delamination. Most EIFS manufacturer warranties are voided by colors with LRV <20.
failure_modes.prevention: EIFS color selection MUST have LRV >20 (preferably >50). Document LRV on project record. Reject dark color requests on EIFS — explain warranty and failure risk. This constraint does NOT apply to traditional stucco.
failure_modes.detection: Fine crazing pattern on south/west-facing EIFS walls. Base coat cracks following EPS board joints. Finish coat separation. Surface feels excessively hot in direct sun.

notes_for_materials_manager: TWO COATING SYSTEM BRANCHES with a HARD CONSTRAINT: (1) Elastomeric (12-20 mils DFT, >300% elongation, 100-175 SF/gal) for traditional stucco ONLY. (2) 100% Acrylic (4-6 mils DFT, flexible, vapor permeable, 200-350 SF/gal) for BOTH traditional stucco and EIFS. When substrate_type = EIFS, coating_system MUST be locked to acrylic — elastomeric is PROHIBITED.

PRIMER BRANCHES by substrate type: Traditional stucco requires alkali-resistant primer rated to pH 13 (e.g., SW Loxon Masonry Primer, BM Ultra Spec Masonry Primer). EIFS requires 100% acrylic exterior primer — standard acrylic is fine since EIFS is not alkaline. Standard interior primer is NOT suitable for either.

Texture profile drives material consumption multiplier (RC-006): smooth 300-350 SF/gal (baseline), sand 200-250 SF/gal (1.25x), lace 150-200 SF/gal (1.50x), dash/roughcast 75-125 SF/gal (2.00x). These rates apply to acrylic topcoat — elastomeric rates are lower due to higher DFT requirement.
Roller nap selection by texture: smooth 3/4-1 inch, sand 1-1/4 inch, lace 1-1/4 inch, dash/roughcast 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch. Nylon/polyester blend for all water-based products.

Spray tip for stucco topcoat: 517, 619, 621 (0.017-0.021 orifice) for acrylic. Elastomeric requires heavier tip (0.021-0.025 orifice) and 2,300-3,000 PSI. 60-mesh (black) filter for acrylic, 30-mesh (gray/coarse) for elastomeric.
Spray application adds 25-33% material waste over brush/roll baseline. Factor into material quantities for spray_backroll method.
Elastomeric caulk for crack patching (<1/8 inch cracks): polyurethane or elastomeric sealant. Must cure before coating (3-7 days for polyurethane, 24-48 hours for latex-based).
Caulk for stucco-to-trim joints: polyurethane (Class 25/50) or hybrid MS polymer. Requires 3-7 day cure before painting if polyurethane.
Mildew treatment materials: household bleach (sodium hypochlorite), TSP, stiff bristle brushes. Bleach solution ratio: 1:3 bleach to water.
Masking tape for stucco: Red stucco poly tape (7.0 mil, 30-day UV rating) for textured stucco surfaces. Standard blue tape will not adhere to textured stucco.

Oil-based and alkyd products are PROHIBITED on stucco (both traditional and EIFS) — include as a material blocker rule. Saponification risk on traditional stucco; incompatibility with EIFS acrylic finish.
EIFS LRV constraint: all finish colors on EIFS must have LRV >20 (preferably >50). Document LRV value on material selection record. This constraint does NOT apply to traditional stucco.
notes_for_sop_librarian: Module structure: setup -> protect -> clean -> prep -> prime -> apply -> cleanup -> teardown. No block fill module (unlike masonry CMU).
Crack assessment task is FIRST in prep sequence — must inspect entire surface and classify all cracks. Cracks >1/8 inch = HARD STOP requiring structural assessment. Document with photos.
EIFS knock test is a mandatory inspection task (QT3/QT4): tap surface systematically to detect hollow areas indicating delamination. Document with photos. Widespread delamination = HARD STOP.

Pressure washing settings BRANCH by substrate_type: traditional stucco 1,500-3,000 PSI standard, EIFS maximum 500 PSI with wide fan tip at 24+ inch distance. Crew must positively identify substrate type BEFORE pressure washing.
Mildew eradication is a conditional prep task — mandatory when mildew is present. Bleach solution 1:3, 15-20 minute dwell, scrub with stiff brush, thorough rinse. Allow to dry completely.
Efflorescence treatment is a conditional prep task for traditional stucco only (EIFS does not effloresce). Cleaning method escalates by severity (water -> TSP -> phosphoric acid).
Cure verification for traditional stucco: verify 30-day cure (standard) or 7-day cure (with Loxon-type primer) before any coating work. Document cure date.
Spray on stucco = ALWAYS add backroll task. No spray-only option. Second technician follows sprayer with appropriate nap roller while coating is wet.
EIFS insurance verification task: verify CGL policy covers EIFS work or obtain EIFS-specific rider BEFORE starting work. Photo documentation of pre-existing conditions is MANDATORY.
Oil-based products are BLOCKED in material selection for this spec. Hard stop if oil-based is selected.
Stucco patch and texture match: patch minor defects with appropriate compound (stucco patch for traditional, manufacturer base coat for EIFS). Allow patch cure time before priming.
Light sand between coats at QT4 only (not QT2 or QT3).
EIFS color selection gate: verify LRV >20 before ordering materials. Document LRV on project record.
notes_for_estimation_engineer: Production rates by texture (spray_backroll, acrylic topcoat): smooth 125-150 SF/hr, sand 80-100 SF/hr, lace 60-80 SF/hr, dash/roughcast 40-60 SF/hr. These are the BASE rates before access modifier.

Texture multiplier is a DUAL modifier (RC-006): affects BOTH labor rate (production SF/hr) AND material consumption (coverage SF/gal). Smooth=1.00x, sand=1.25x, lace=1.50x, dash=2.00x. Apply to both pathways.
Elastomeric topcoat rates are approximately 60-75% of acrylic rates due to heavier material and higher DFT (12-20 mils vs 4-6 mils).
Access modifier (FAC_EXT_ACCESS): ground=1.00, ladder=1.35, scaffold=1.60, lift=1.50. Applied per elevation based on working height.

Material coverage: acrylic on smooth stucco 300-350 SF/gal, acrylic on sand 200-250 SF/gal, acrylic on lace 150-200 SF/gal, acrylic on dash 75-125 SF/gal. Elastomeric on smooth 150-175 SF/gal, elastomeric on textured significantly lower.
Primer application rate (spray_backroll): 300-450 SF/hr for alkali-resistant primer on traditional stucco, 350-500 SF/hr for standard acrylic primer on EIFS (smoother substrate, less absorption).
Crack patching rate: 50-100 LF/hr depending on crack width and depth.
Pressure wash rate: traditional stucco 400-600 SF/hr, EIFS 200-350 SF/hr (slower due to low-pressure requirement and careful technique).
Mildew treatment: 100-200 SF/hr depending on severity.
Stucco patch and texture match: 50-100 SF/hr for patching defects.
Environmental conditions (wind, dew point, sun, surface temp) are EXCLUDED from estimation — they are SOP/process concerns, not estimatable at bid time (RC-002).
Coat system: 1 primer + 2 finish coats standard at QT3/QT4. QT2 may use single finish coat on properly primed surface.
Caulk stucco-to-trim joints: 75-150 LF/hr depending on joint complexity.
Scaffold setup/teardown for stucco: 1.75-2.5 hrs setup per facade, 1.0-1.5 hrs teardown per facade (2-person crew). Must be a distinct line item.
Masking-to-spray ratio: 3:1 to 4:1 (masking hours to spray hours). Masking is a separate line item.
EIFS knock test inspection: fixed time per elevation (~0.5-1.0 hr per elevation), not area-scaled.
No FAC_EXT_SUBSTRATE_CONDITION modifier — NC spec has no condition variation. State routing handled by substrate_state_rules (RC-004).

assumptions.value: New construction stucco and EIFS exterior wall coating. Wall field surfaces only.
assumptions.note: Trim around stucco openings is covered by separate exterior trim spec. Foundation coatings below grade are excluded.

assumptions.value: Two substrate types: traditional 3-coat stucco (Portland cement/sand/lime) and EIFS/synthetic stucco (EPS + polymer base + acrylic finish).
assumptions.note: These are fundamentally different materials with different coating requirements. Must be treated as a configuration dimension with hard constraint rules.

assumptions.value: Mandatory on all spray-applied stucco coatings. No spray-only option.
assumptions.note: Explicit doctrine guidance: stucco texture requires back-rolling to force coating into recesses for continuous film.

assumptions.value: Elastomeric coatings are PROHIBITED on EIFS — hard blocker rule enforced at material selection.
assumptions.note: This is the most critical constraint rule in this spec. EIFS + elastomeric = catastrophic moisture entrapment failure.

assumptions.value: QT5 not applicable to stucco wall field applications.
assumptions.source: Sibling spec pattern (masonry, fiber cement, wood siding)
assumptions.note: QT5 reserved for fine exterior millwork, columns, decorative elements. Not wall field surfaces.

assumptions.value: This spec covers new construction only. Single substrate state (SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY).
assumptions.note: SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY is correct for both traditional stucco and EIFS in NC context — stucco is cementitious and EIFS arrives uncoated. Repaint states would require a separate spec.

assumptions.value: Stucco does NOT require block filler (unlike CMU masonry). Stucco surface is continuous — no block voids to fill.
assumptions.note: Block filler is a CMU-specific requirement. Traditional stucco and EIFS have continuous surface profiles that do not require void filling.

assumptions.value: Landscape protection measured in LF (perimeter), NOT SF (area).
assumptions.note: Same correction applied in all prior exterior specs. Perimeter-based measurement for drop cloth/tarp placement.

uncertainties.topic: Elastomeric coverage rate on textured stucco
uncertainties.detail: Elastomeric coatings at 12-20 mils DFT on textured stucco consume significantly more material than acrylic. Doctrine provides acrylic coverage rates by texture but does not specify exact elastomeric rates by texture profile. The interaction between high DFT and rough texture creates exponential material consumption.
uncertainties.recommendation: Use elastomeric baseline of 100-175 SF/gal on smooth, apply texture multiplier (sand 1.25x, lace 1.50x, dash 2.00x) to derive textured rates. Flag for field calibration.

uncertainties.detail: EIFS patch repairs use manufacturer-specified base coat compounds with variable cure times (24 hours to 7 days depending on product, thickness, and conditions). Doctrine says 'per manufacturer' without specifying a standard.
uncertainties.recommendation: Default to 48-hour cure for EIFS patches. Note as SOP procedure item, not estimation factor.

uncertainties.topic: Traditional stucco vs EIFS identification in field
uncertainties.detail: Some crew members may not reliably distinguish traditional stucco from EIFS, especially when both are painted. Misidentification leads to wrong pressure wash settings and wrong coating system. Knock test helps but is not foolproof.
uncertainties.recommendation: Include positive substrate identification as first task in SOP. Check building plans or tap test: EIFS sounds hollow, traditional stucco sounds solid. Document substrate type with photo evidence.

uncertainties.detail: Spanish lace texture varies significantly in depth and pattern density. The 60-80 SF/hr range reflects this variability, but particularly deep lace patterns may fall below 60 SF/hr.
uncertainties.recommendation: Use 70 SF/hr as midpoint for lace texture. Flag deep lace patterns for field rate adjustment.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray_backroll
zones.notes: LF-based (RC-003) — measured along house perimeter where landscape is adjacent. Roll: drop cloth at base. Spray_backroll: full tarp width over plantings.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray_backroll
zones.notes: Adjacent walkways. Roll: drop cloth runners. Spray_backroll: full tarp coverage.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray_backroll
zones.notes: Adjacent patio surfaces. Protection level driven by proximity and application method.
Exterior light fixtures mounted on or adjacent to stucco wall. Bag or tape over fixture.
HVAC condenser units adjacent to stucco wall. Full tarp cover during spray operations. Shutdown protocol per Protection Doctrine.

protection_zones_analysis.cross_spec_protection_note: Window and door protection during stucco wall work is NOT this spec's responsibility. Window/door masking belongs in the respective window or door spec. This prevents double-counting and ensures protection responsibility is clear per surface owner.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Window casing or stucco pop-out trim at openings. Stucco terminates at opening. No cut-in — trim is a separate spec.
Door casing trim. Same as window casing relationship. Separate spec.
Soffit underside at eave junction. Often different color. Separate scope.
Foundation below stucco wall. Not painted in this scope. Drop cloth protection at grade level.
Frieze or band board at stucco-to-soffit junction (if present). Separate trim scope.

adjacency_analysis.key_finding: Stucco wall field has NO edge work requirements within this spec. All adjacent surfaces are separate specs (trim, soffit, foundation) or not in scope. Protection relationships only. Stucco terminates at openings and trim elements. Window/door protection owned by window/door specs.

affected_conditions.notes: Access type drives a HEIGHT MODIFIER on tasks. Applied per elevation based on working height. Scaffold common for multi-story stucco.

excluded_conditions.rationale: Environmental conditions are important to the painting PROCESS but are NOT estimatable. They are unpredictable, change daily, and cannot be set as fixed conditions for an estimate. They belong in SOP procedure notes and job-site decision protocols, not in production rate modifiers (RC-002).

excluded.reason: Unpredictable. Changes hourly. Cannot set a fixed modifier for estimate.
Varies by time of day, sun angle, and season. Not predictable at bid time.
Weather-dependent. Not predictable at bid time.
Varies by elevation and season. Scheduling concern, not estimation.

valid_input_states.rationale: NC stucco arrives bare and uncoated. SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY is correct for both traditional stucco (cementitious, alkaline) and EIFS (arrives with factory acrylic finish that is intended to be topcoated). Single substrate state simplifies this NC spec (RC-001).

output_state.rationale: Output state is the painted finish. Flat is the most common exterior stucco sheen (hides texture irregularities, traditional appearance). Actual output varies by sheen configuration (flat, satin). Satin more common on EIFS for easier cleaning.

adjacent_state_protection_analysis.rationale: Protect finished trim from stucco spray overspray. Unfinished trim needs no protection — it will be painted later.
Soffit is typically painted before walls (top-down sequencing). If already finished, light masking at the wall-soffit junction.
Foundation wall is rarely painted in NC context. Drop cloth at grade level handled by landscape/hardscape protection zones.

exterior_substrate_states.description: New, uncoated stucco surface. Traditional stucco: highly alkaline (pH up to 13), requires alkali-resistant primer. EIFS: non-alkaline acrylic finish, requires 100% acrylic primer. Both arrive uncoated in NC context.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Traditional stucco: verify cure age (30 days standard, 7 days minimum with Loxon-type primer), moisture test (MC < 12%), treat efflorescence if present, patch cracks <1/8 inch, crack assessment (>1/8 inch = hard stop). EIFS: knock test for delamination, low-pressure wash only, verify LRV >20 for color selection, insurance verification.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: Traditional stucco: alkali-resistant primer rated to pH 13 (e.g., SW Loxon Masonry Primer). EIFS: 100% acrylic exterior primer (standard acrylic is suitable — no alkalinity concern).
exterior_substrate_states.notes: This is the only NC state for stucco. Both substrate types arrive bare/uncoated. The critical difference is in primer selection (alkali-resistant vs standard acrylic) and topcoat selection (elastomeric allowed vs prohibited). RC-001 confirms SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY is correct.

exterior_access_type_analysis.treatment: Modifier on tasks, not a site condition. Same concept as FAC_HEIGHT for interior.

scenarios.notes: Single-story stucco, first 8 ft. No ladder needed. Baseline rate.
Two-story stucco, areas above 8 ft. Constant repositioning. Safety overhead.
Preferred for multi-story stucco — long continuous runs at height. Better ergonomics for spray_backroll operations. Setup/teardown is a separate line item.
Boom/scissor lift for 3+ story or difficult access. Requires firm ground. Rental cost.

exterior_environmental_constraints.note: Environmental constraints are documented here for SOP reference but are EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers per established exterior spec convention (RC-002).

sop_reference_only.note: Below 50: slow cure, adhesion risk. Above 90: improper cure, flash drying, bubbling. EIFS surface temp can exceed ambient by 30-50 degrees F in direct sun due to insulation backing.

sop_reference_only.rule: Surface temp must be >= 5 degrees F above dew point
sop_reference_only.note: Adhesion and blushing risk at marginal conditions.

sop_reference_only.rule: Traditional stucco MC < 12% (hard stop). EIFS: surface dry to touch, no visible moisture.
sop_reference_only.note: Test traditional stucco with electronic moisture meter. EIFS moisture assessment is primarily visual and tactile.

sop_reference_only.rule: Traditional stucco: 30 days standard, 7 days minimum with alkali-resistant primer. EIFS: per manufacturer spec (typically 24-48 hours for base coat cure).
sop_reference_only.note: New traditional stucco pH up to 13. Must verify cure age before any coating work.

spray_backroll_acrylic_smooth.notes: Baseline stucco rate. Smooth finish. Spray with immediate backroll (3/4-1 inch nap). 2-person crew.

spray_backroll_acrylic_sand.notes: Sand texture. 1.25x labor multiplier over smooth. 1-1/4 inch nap roller.

spray_backroll_acrylic_lace.notes: Spanish lace texture. 1.50x labor multiplier over smooth. Deep recesses require careful backroll. 1-1/4 inch nap.

spray_backroll_acrylic_dash.notes: Dash/roughcast texture. 2.00x labor multiplier over smooth. Highest material consumption. 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch nap.

spray_backroll_elastomeric_smooth.notes: Elastomeric on smooth traditional stucco. ~65% of acrylic rate. Heavier material, higher DFT (12-20 mils). Heavy-duty tip.

spray_backroll_elastomeric_textured.notes: Elastomeric on textured traditional stucco. Apply texture multiplier to smooth elastomeric base rate.

roll_acrylic_smooth.notes: Roller only on smooth stucco. 3/4-1 inch nap. Good mechanical bond.

roll_acrylic_textured.notes: Roller only on textured stucco. Rate varies significantly by texture depth. 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch nap.

brush.notes: Detail work, small areas, patches only. Not a primary method for stucco wall field.

alkali_resistant_primer_spray_backroll.notes: Primer on bare traditional stucco. Spray + backroll (mandatory). Primer is thinner bodied than topcoat.

acrylic_primer_spray_backroll_eifs.notes: Standard acrylic primer on EIFS. Smoother substrate, less absorption than traditional stucco.

pressure_wash_traditional.notes: 1,500-3,000 PSI water wash for traditional stucco.

pressure_wash_eifs.notes: Low-pressure wash for EIFS (<500 PSI, wide fan, 24+ inch distance). Slower due to care required.

mildew_treatment.notes: Bleach solution application, dwell, scrub, rinse. Rate depends on severity.

efflorescence_treatment_light.notes: Traditional stucco only. Water + stiff brush. Light salt deposits.

efflorescence_treatment_acid.notes: Traditional stucco only. Acid wash + neutralization. Severe deposits.

crack_patching.notes: Cosmetic cracks <1/8 inch. Elastomeric caulk fill. Rate depends on crack density.

stucco_patch_texture_match.notes: Patching defects and matching existing texture. Slower for complex textures (lace, dash).

caulk_stucco_joints.notes: Stucco-to-trim joint caulking. Gun + finger tool.

crack_assessment.notes: Fixed time per elevation. Walk entire surface, classify all cracks, photo document.

eifs_knock_test.notes: Fixed time per elevation. Systematic tap test across entire EIFS surface. Photo document.

moisture_testing.notes: Fixed time per project. Electronic meter readings at multiple locations. Traditional stucco only.

key_decisions.decision: Combined (full phase_scope). Prime and finish phases have unique task keys within the single spec.
key_decisions.rationale: NC stucco painting is a single-mobilization scope — same crew primes and paints. Each phase (prime, finish) has its own task IDs and module IDs for independent rate tracking. Matches masonry and siding sibling spec pattern.

key_decisions.topic: Substrate type as primary branching dimension
key_decisions.rationale: Substrate type is the PRIMARY branching dimension for this spec. It drives coating system compatibility (hard constraint), primer selection, pressure wash settings, LRV constraints, and insurance requirements. The two substrates share a visual category but are fundamentally different materials.

key_decisions.topic: Coating system as configuration dimension with hard constraint
key_decisions.decision: Include coating_system dimension: elastomeric, acrylic. HARD CONSTRAINT: when substrate_type = EIFS, coating_system MUST be locked to acrylic (RC-005).
key_decisions.rationale: Elastomeric on EIFS causes catastrophic moisture entrapment failure. This is not a recommendation — it is a PROHIBITION. The constraint must be enforced at the configuration level so that elastomeric + EIFS is an invalid combination that cannot be selected.

key_decisions.topic: Texture profile as configuration dimension with dual multiplier
key_decisions.decision: Include texture_profile dimension: smooth, sand, lace, dash. Texture drives BOTH labor rate and material consumption multipliers (RC-006).
key_decisions.rationale: Texture is the dominant production and material cost driver for stucco. Smooth=1.00x baseline, sand=1.25x, lace=1.50x, dash=2.00x. The multiplier applies to BOTH SF/hr (labor) AND SF/gal (material). Both pathways are needed for accurate estimation.

key_decisions.decision: Application method 'spray_backroll' is a single unit — there is no spray-only option for stucco.
key_decisions.rationale: Per Exterior Application Methods Doctrine: spray on textured stucco mandates back-rolling to force coating into texture recesses. The 'spray_backroll' method is treated as a single production rate, not two separate tasks.

key_decisions.decision: EIFS color selection requires LRV >20 (preferably >50). This is a configuration constraint, not a coating system property.
key_decisions.rationale: Dark colors (LRV <20) on EIFS cause thermal distress — EPS softens above 165 degrees F. Most EIFS manufacturer warranties void for LRV <20. Traditional stucco has no LRV constraint.

key_decisions.decision: EIFS substrate triggers a mandatory insurance verification workflow flag. Not an estimation factor — a project management gate.
key_decisions.rationale: CGL policies commonly exclude EIFS. Must verify coverage or obtain rider before starting work. Photo documentation mandatory. This is surfaced in the project workflow, not in the estimate.

key_decisions.decision: Oil-based and alkyd products are PROHIBITED for this spec. Hard blocker rule.
key_decisions.rationale: Saponification on alkaline traditional stucco is catastrophic. Oil-based is also incompatible with EIFS acrylic systems. Block at material selection stage — no exceptions.

Both traditional stucco and EIFS arrive bare/uncoated in NC. SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY is the correct state for cementitious substrates. Repaint states (sound existing, failed existing) would require a separate spec.

key_decisions.decision: Stucco does NOT require block filler (unlike CMU masonry).
key_decisions.rationale: Stucco has a continuous surface profile — no block voids to fill. Block filler module from masonry spec is not carried over.

key_decisions.decision: NOT this spec's responsibility. Per established exterior spec convention.
key_decisions.rationale: Window/door protection belongs in window/door specs. Prevents double-counting. Clear ownership per surface.

key_decisions.decision: EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers. Per established exterior spec convention (RC-002).
key_decisions.rationale: Environmental conditions are unpredictable at bid time. They are SOP/process concerns documented for field reference but not included in production rate modifiers.

key_decisions.decision: 1 primer + 2 finish coats standard at QT3/QT4. QT2 may accept single finish coat on properly primed surface.
key_decisions.rationale: Stucco requires dedicated primer (alkali-resistant for traditional, acrylic for EIFS). Two topcoats provide proper DFT and film build for durability.

key_decisions.topic: Crack assessment as mandatory first task
key_decisions.decision: Crack assessment is the FIRST task in the prep sequence. Cracks >1/8 inch = HARD STOP.
key_decisions.rationale: Structural cracks must be identified before any coating work begins. Coating over structural cracks is a liability issue and a coating failure guarantee.

key_decisions.topic: No substrate condition modifier for NC
key_decisions.decision: No FAC_EXT_SUBSTRATE_CONDITION modifier. NC spec has no condition variation (RC-004).
key_decisions.rationale: All NC stucco arrives in the same base condition (bare). Condition variation is a repaint concern. State routing is handled by substrate_state_rules, not a condition modifier.

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Primary branching dimension. Drives coating system constraint (elastomeric prohibited on EIFS), primer selection, pressure wash settings, LRV constraints, and insurance requirements. Not captured by existing PS keys.
proposed_new_keys.notes: Per-elevation if mixed substrate types on same structure (rare but possible in additions or mixed-material facades).

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Drives dual multiplier on labor rate (SF/hr) and material consumption (SF/gal). The dominant cost driver for stucco estimation. Not captured by existing PS keys.
proposed_new_keys.notes: Per-elevation if texture varies (uncommon in NC but possible). Texture multipliers: smooth 1.00x, sand 1.25x, lace 1.50x, dash 2.00x.

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Drives DFT, material consumption, production rate, and compatibility constraint with substrate_type. HARD RULE: EIFS = acrylic only.
proposed_new_keys.notes: Project-level configuration. Elastomeric selection triggers moisture source assessment documentation requirement and is invalid when substrate_type = EIFS.

proposed_new_keys.rationale: CGL policies commonly exclude EIFS. This flag tracks whether insurance verification is complete. Required before starting EIFS work.
proposed_new_keys.notes: Workflow flag only — does not affect estimation. Surfaced in project management workflow.

research_corrections.correction: SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY is the correct substrate state for both traditional stucco and EIFS in NC context. Traditional stucco is cementitious (Portland cement base) — same chemical family as masonry. EIFS arrives with factory acrylic finish intended for topcoating, effectively 'bare' from a painting perspective.
research_corrections.impact: Confirms single-state simplification for NC spec.

research_corrections.correction: Environmental conditions (wind, dew point, sun, surface temperature) are EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers. They are process/scheduling concerns, not estimatable at bid time. Documented for SOP reference only. This follows the established pattern from RC-003 in the fiber cement sibling spec.
research_corrections.source: Established exterior spec convention; fiber cement sibling RC-003
research_corrections.impact: No environmental modifier factors in estimation engine. SOP reference only.

research_corrections.topic: Landscape protection uses LF not SF
research_corrections.correction: Landscape protection is measured in LF (perimeter along house where landscape is adjacent), NOT SF (area). This is the same correction applied in all prior exterior specs. Drop cloth/tarp placement is a linear measurement along the perimeter, not an area measurement.
research_corrections.source: Established exterior spec convention; all prior exterior sibling specs

research_corrections.topic: No substrate condition modifier for NC
research_corrections.correction: No FAC_EXT_SUBSTRATE_CONDITION modifier exists for this NC spec. There is no condition variation in new construction — all NC stucco arrives in the same base condition (bare). Substrate state routing is handled by substrate_state_rules, not by a condition modifier factor.
research_corrections.impact: Eliminates unnecessary condition modifier from estimation engine.

research_corrections.correction: When substrate_type = EIFS, coating_system MUST be locked to acrylic. Elastomeric is PROHIBITED on EIFS — this is a hard constraint rule enforced at the configuration level, not a recommendation. Elastomeric on EIFS causes catastrophic moisture entrapment and system failure. The constraint must make the combination (EIFS + elastomeric) an invalid, unselectable configuration.
research_corrections.impact: Configuration-level blocker rule. EIFS + elastomeric = invalid combination.

research_corrections.correction: Texture profile multiplier affects BOTH labor rate (production SF/hr) AND material consumption (coverage SF/gal). This is a DUAL multiplier — rougher textures slow production AND increase material usage. Both pathways must be implemented in the estimation engine. Smooth=1.00x, sand=1.25x, lace=1.50x, dash=2.00x applies to both labor and material calculations.
research_corrections.impact: Estimation engine must apply texture multiplier to BOTH SF/hr rates AND SF/gal coverage rates.
